issues.legal_issue: A government delegate cannot review and set aside the government’s earlier order unless the government has power to review that order, and an operative order cannot be ignored unless set aside or declared void by a competent authority.
material_facts: The government had set aside earlier administrative decisions and remanded the matters for reconsideration.
A later commissioner, acting as the government’s delegate, set aside the government’s earlier order on the ground that it had been made without legal authority.
No provision conferring review power on the government, either expressly or by necessary implication, was identified.
The government’s earlier order had not been set aside or declared void by a competent authority.
issues.conclusion: The commissioner lacked competence to review and set aside the government’s earlier order. The commissioner’s order was liable to be set aside, and the operative earlier order could not be ignored by subordinate tribunals.
issues.legal_principle: The power to review is not inherent and must be conferred by law, expressly or by necessary implication. A delegate cannot exercise a review power that the government itself does not possess. An order remains binding on subordinate tribunals unless it is set aside or declared void by a competent authority. The Court identified no provision of the Saurashtra Land Reforms Act conferring review power; it did not decide whether Section 63(2) authorized the government to entertain the earlier revision application. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_judgment and officer_acting_as_government_delegate and officer_set_aside_government_order and government_lacked_review_power and original_order_not_set_aside_by_competent_authority

predicates.appeal_from_writ_judgment: The proceeding is an appeal from a judgment reviewing an administrative order.
predicates.officer_acting_as_government_delegate: An officer acted as a delegate of the government.
predicates.officer_set_aside_government_order: The officer purported to review and set aside an earlier order made by the government.
predicates.government_lacked_review_power: No law conferred on the government, expressly or by necessary implication, power to review the earlier order.
predicates.original_order_not_set_aside_by_competen: The earlier government order had not been set aside or declared void by a competent authority.

issues.definition: When an officer acting as a government delegate sets aside an earlier government order without the government having review power, and that earlier order has not been set aside by a competent authority, the delegate’s review order is without authority.
